projections.text: On January 30, 2016, the New York City Council held a constituent-services hackathon at Civic Hall. Civic Hall announced the session for 1-3 p.m.

boundaries: Do not describe the Wayback page as a recovered event calendar listing.

projections.text: The Council described the gathering as its first CouncilStat hackathon.
After the fuller CouncilStat dataset was released, Jamie developed CallNYC.org as an independent public-facing interpretation of those constituent-services records.
Built an independent civic-data follow-on translating CouncilStat constituent-services records into resident-facing issue pathways and next-step guidance.

Built CallNYC.org as an independent follow-on to the New York City Council's first CouncilStat hackathon, translating constituent-services data into resident-facing issue pages and next-step guidance; covered in Politico New York.

supports: sequence from the January event through the fuller data release
surviving implementation of the independent prototype

boundaries: CallNYC was an independent follow-on, not an official Council product, documented formal submission, or winner.

projections.text: CallNYC is an archived independent prototype, not an official or current New York City Council service.

boundaries: Historical officeholders, statistics, categories, and contact information are not current guidance.

projections.text: A 2017 Greene Hill Food Co-op profile described the dinners as weekly and open to the community.

supports: Jamie and Julie's shared hosting role

boundaries: This source does not establish the total gathering count or complete project duration.

projections.text: A 2017 Greene Hill Food Co-op profile described WOW List as a place where Jamie and Julie shared community events.

supports: Jamie and Julie's public association with the project

boundaries: The profile does not establish user, event, or city-scale metrics.

projections.text: On October 22, 2018, I testified before the New York City Council as an NYC Artist Coalition member in support of Intro 737 and commercial rent protections for cultural spaces.

supports: support for Intro 737 and commercial rent protections

boundaries: Public testimony does not establish legislative authorship, passage, or sole campaign leadership.

projections.text: I co-led planning and public-benefit documentation for the proposed mixed-use rehabilitation.
Co-led planning and public-benefit documentation for a proposed mixed-use rehabilitation.

boundaries: This is approved resume-backed role language; municipal records separately corroborate the proposal and presenter details, not the complete division of labor.

projections.text: In June 2019, Kansas City public minutes identified me as KC Town Hall's presenter for a $490,539 proposal to renovate a building at 36th and Indiana into four retail spaces and three apartments.
Presented the $490,539 proposal in Kansas City's public funding process.

boundaries: A proposal and public funding recommendation are not completed construction or final funds received.

projections.text: On September 26, 2019, the Kansas City Council accepted the CCED Board's recommendation of up to $490,539 for KC Town Hall and authorized funding-agreement negotiations.

supports: acceptance of the CCED Board recommendation

boundaries: Acceptance and negotiation authority do not establish an executed agreement, payment, construction, or Jamie's sole causality.

projections.text: At the same meeting, the Council passed Ordinance 190642, appropriating $490,539 to KC Town Hall in the Round Two project table.
The Council accepted the CCED recommendation and appropriated $490,539 for the project; this did not establish disbursement or completed construction.

boundaries: The appropriation does not establish payment, disbursement, an executed agreement, construction, or Jamie's sole causality.

projections.text: A May 2022 city status report still listed the funding agreement in negotiation and reported no disbursement amount at that point.

supports: a dash in the Funds Disbursed column

boundaries: This is a dated interim status record; it does not by itself establish the project's status after May 17, 2022.

projections.text: A 2024 Kansas City ordinance records that KC Town Hall withdrew and would no longer proceed under that award; the unused $490,539 was reappropriated.
The project later withdrew before proceeding under the award, and the unused allocation was reappropriated.

boundaries: The ordinance does not state the reasons for withdrawal or assign fault.

projections.text: After the project stopped proceeding under the CCED award, I transitioned it to a mission-aligned organization.
Jamie subsequently transitioned the project to a mission-aligned organization.

boundaries: Jamie's first-person confirmation supports the transition and broad recipient description, not the organization's identity, the transition's legal form or date, any transfer of public funds or property, the project's current status, or the circumstances that led to the transition.
The municipal withdrawal and reappropriation records do not document this separate transition.
